questions.question: In a DDPM-style forward noising process with variance schedule {\beta_t} and \(\alpha_t = 1-\beta_t\), what is the marginal distribution of \(x_t\) given the clean data \(x_0\)?
questions.choice_A: Gaussian with mean \(\sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_t}\, x_0\) and covariance \((1-\bar{\alpha}_t)\,\mathbf{I}\), where \(\bar{\alpha}_t=\prod_{s=1}^t \alpha_s\)
questions.choice_B: Gaussian with mean \(x_0\) and covariance \(t\,\mathbf{I}\)
questions.choice_C: A heavy-tailed distribution whose variance depends on \(\sum_{s=1}^t \beta_s\) but is not Gaussian
questions.choice_D: A mixture of Gaussians centered at \(x_0\) with variances given by \(\beta_t\)

questions.question: In score-based generative modeling, what does the score function \(\nabla_x \log p_t(x)\) represent and how is it used in reverse-time dynamics?
questions.choice_A: It is the gradient of the data log-likelihood and is used to train the encoder in an autoencoder
questions.choice_B: It is the gradient of the log-density of the noised data at time \(t\) and appears as a guiding drift term in the reverse SDE/ODE
questions.choice_C: It is the Laplacian of the log-density and controls the diffusion coefficient in the forward SDE
questions.choice_D: It is a constant vector field that enforces stability of the numerical solver

questions.question: Why do DDPMs commonly train a network to predict the noise \(\varepsilon\) added at time \(t\), rather than directly predicting \(x_0\)?
questions.choice_A: Predicting \(x_0\) makes the loss non-convex and unstable across all timesteps
questions.choice_B: Predicting noise is necessary to compute the ELBO
questions.choice_C: Predicting noise yields a simple, well-scaled MSE objective aligned with the Gaussian corruption model and is equivalent (up to reparameterization) to predicting \(x_0\) under appropriate weighting
questions.choice_D: Predicting noise completely removes the need for a variance schedule

questions.question: Under the standard DDPM formulation with fixed variance (or learned variance with stop-gradient), which statement about the training objective is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: It is a cross-entropy term encouraging the classifier to separate clean and noisy samples
questions.choice_B: It is a Wasserstein distance between the forward and reverse processes
questions.choice_C: It is an adversarial loss comparing the generator and discriminator over timesteps
questions.choice_D: It reduces to a weighted mean-squared error on the predicted noise across timesteps, corresponding to a variational bound on log-likelihood

questions.question: Which distinction best characterizes ancestral sampling (DDPM) versus DDIM sampling?
questions.choice_A: Ancestral sampling is stochastic and Markovian with per-step noise injection, whereas DDIM can be deterministic by using a non-Markovian update that preserves the same marginals
questions.choice_B: Ancestral sampling requires a classifier, whereas DDIM does not
questions.choice_C: DDIM trains a different network architecture than DDPM
questions.choice_D: Ancestral sampling is only applicable in latent space, whereas DDIM is only applicable in pixel space

questions.question: How is classifier-free guidance typically implemented in diffusion models for conditional generation?
questions.choice_A: By adding random Gaussian noise to the conditional embedding during training
questions.choice_B: By combining unconditional and conditional scores (or noise predictions) as \(s_{\text{guided}} = s_{\text{uncond}} + w\,(s_{\text{cond}} - s_{\text{uncond}})\) with guidance scale \(w\)
questions.choice_C: By training a separate diffusion model for each class and averaging their outputs
questions.choice_D: By setting the diffusion variance \(\beta_t\) to zero at test time

questions.question: What is the probability flow ODE in the context of score-based SDEs?
questions.choice_A: An ODE that approximates the forward SDE by ignoring diffusion terms while changing the marginal distributions
questions.choice_B: A reverse-time SDE with increased diffusion that accelerates sampling
questions.choice_C: An ODE whose trajectories share the same time marginals as the forward SDE and enable deterministic sampling using the learned score
questions.choice_D: An ODE used only for training that cannot be used for sampling

questions.question: What is a practical consequence of choosing an overly aggressive \(\beta_t\) schedule early in the diffusion process?
questions.choice_A: The reverse process becomes more stable and easier to integrate numerically
questions.choice_B: The model learns better representations because the signal is destroyed quickly
questions.choice_C: The ELBO becomes tighter due to lower Kullback–Leibler divergences at early steps
questions.choice_D: The signal-to-noise ratio collapses too quickly, making it harder for the model to learn from early timesteps and potentially hurting sample quality

questions.question: What is the primary motivation for latent diffusion as opposed to pixel-space diffusion?
questions.choice_A: To perform denoising in a lower-dimensional, perceptually aligned latent space that reduces compute while retaining semantic content via a learned autoencoder
questions.choice_B: To avoid learning any decoder, thereby removing reconstruction error
questions.choice_C: To guarantee exact likelihood computation during sampling
questions.choice_D: To eliminate the need for timestep conditioning

questions.question: How can likelihood be estimated in continuous-time score-based models if one wishes to evaluate log-likelihood on data?
questions.choice_A: By counting the number of denoising steps that reach the data manifold
questions.choice_B: By integrating the instantaneous change-of-variables along the probability flow ODE and estimating divergence terms, e.g., with Hutchinson’s trace estimator
questions.choice_C: By training a separate normalizing flow on the model samples
questions.choice_D: It is impossible to estimate likelihood in these models

questions.question: What is the rationale behind the "v-prediction" parameterization used in some diffusion models (predicting \(v = \alpha_t x_0 + \sigma_t \varepsilon\))?
questions.choice_A: It changes the architecture to a variational autoencoder during sampling
questions.choice_B: It forces the model to predict the clean image exactly at all timesteps
questions.choice_C: It provides a better-conditioned target that smoothly interpolates between predicting \(x_0\) and \(\varepsilon\), improving training stability across signal-to-noise regimes
questions.choice_D: It eliminates the need for noise schedules altogether

questions.question: Which expression best captures the relationship between the reverse-time dynamics and the score function for a variance-exploding SDE?
questions.choice_A: The reverse-time drift equals the forward-time drift
questions.choice_B: The reverse-time SDE removes the score term entirely and doubles the diffusion
questions.choice_C: The reverse-time diffusion coefficient is negated but the drift is unchanged
questions.choice_D: The reverse-time SDE adds a drift term proportional to the score, typically of the form \(\mathrm{d}x = [f(x,t) - g(t)^2 \nabla_x \log p_t(x)]\,\mathrm{d}t + g(t)\,\mathrm{d}\bar{w}\)

questions.question: Recent work proposes alternative noise level schedules such as cosine schedules. What is a key intended benefit of such schedules compared to linear \(\beta_t\)?
questions.choice_A: They maintain a more uniform signal-to-noise ratio over timesteps, easing learning and improving sample quality
questions.choice_B: They guarantee faster convergence in wall-clock time
questions.choice_C: They remove the need for timestep embeddings
questions.choice_D: They make the forward process non-Gaussian

questions.question: How does classifier guidance differ from classifier-free guidance in diffusion sampling?
questions.choice_A: Classifier guidance uses an unconditional model only, while classifier-free uses a classifier
questions.choice_B: Classifier guidance uses gradients of an external classifier’s \(\log p(y\mid x_t)\) with respect to \(x_t\), which can introduce adversarial artifacts; classifier-free guidance blends conditional and unconditional diffusion predictions from the same model
questions.choice_C: They are identical methods with different names
questions.choice_D: Classifier-free guidance requires labeled data at test time, whereas classifier guidance does not

questions.question: In DDPMs, what is the form of the true posterior \(q(x_{t-1}\mid x_t, x_0)\) and how is it used in training or sampling?
questions.choice_A: It is uniform over a sphere around \(x_t\) and is only used for evaluation
questions.choice_B: It is a Dirac delta at \(x_0\) and is never used in practice
questions.choice_C: It is Gaussian with a mean that depends linearly on both \(x_t\) and \(x_0\); at test time, \(x_0\) is replaced by the model’s estimate to form the reverse transition
questions.choice_D: It is a mixture of Gaussians over all previous timesteps

questions.question: What role does the stochasticity parameter \(\eta\) play in DDIM sampling?
questions.choice_A: It controls the learning rate of the optimizer during training
questions.choice_B: It scales the classifier-free guidance strength
questions.choice_C: It determines the number of timesteps used during sampling
questions.choice_D: It controls the amount of noise injected per step, with \(\eta=0\) yielding deterministic DDIM and larger \(\eta\) recovering stochastic behavior closer to DDPM

questions.question: Why is an exponential moving average (EMA) of model parameters often used for sampling in diffusion models?
questions.choice_A: EMA smooths high-frequency parameter noise accumulated during training, typically yielding more stable and higher-quality samples at test time
questions.choice_B: EMA reduces the number of denoising steps required
questions.choice_C: EMA increases the model capacity without changing architecture
questions.choice_D: EMA is necessary to compute the variational bound

questions.question: What is the purpose of loss weighting schemes based on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) across timesteps?
questions.choice_A: To emphasize only the noisiest steps during training
questions.choice_B: To balance contributions from high- and low-noise regimes so that the model does not overfit easy timesteps or ignore hard ones
questions.choice_C: To replace the need for a timestep embedding in the network
questions.choice_D: To ensure the ELBO equals the true log-likelihood

questions.question: Which statement best captures a key trade-off between latent diffusion and pixel-space diffusion?
questions.choice_A: Pixel-space diffusion always trains faster due to smaller models
questions.choice_B: Latent diffusion cannot represent fine details because the decoder ignores spatial structure
questions.choice_C: Latent diffusion reduces computational cost by operating on compressed features, but overall fidelity depends on the quality of the learned autoencoder and its perceptual losses
questions.choice_D: Pixel-space diffusion cannot be conditioned on text or other modalities

questions.question: Which description best characterizes ancestral versus deterministic samplers in terms of numerical behavior?
questions.choice_A: Deterministic samplers increase variance at each step to reduce bias
questions.choice_B: Ancestral samplers follow an ODE with no stochasticity
questions.choice_C: Deterministic samplers (e.g., probability flow ODE, DDIM with \(\eta=0\)) can use higher-order integrators and often require fewer steps for similar quality, though they may introduce bias relative to the stochastic process
questions.choice_D: Ancestral samplers guarantee lower FID with fewer steps

questions.question: When using higher-order solvers (e.g., Heun’s method, Runge–Kutta) for diffusion ODE/SDE sampling, what is a typical practical consideration?
questions.choice_A: Higher-order solvers remove the need for a noise schedule
questions.choice_B: They guarantee stability regardless of step size
questions.choice_C: They are incompatible with classifier-free guidance
questions.choice_D: They can reduce the number of function evaluations needed for a target quality, but overly large steps can still cause instability or bias in the generated samples
